findings.title: Accidental git submodule (gitlink) added without .gitmodules
findings.body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290...`, i.e. a git submodule/gitlink pointing at the base commit of this same repository, but no `.gitmodules` entry is added. This is almost certainly an accidental commit of a nested checkout. It breaks any workflow that initializes submodules: `git submodule update --init` fails with `fatal: no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path 'sentry-repo'`, which affects CI checkouts that run with `--recurse-submodules` and fresh clones. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) without coalescing NULLs, silently undercounting unsampled errors
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is defined as `toInt64(sum(Column("sample_weight")))`. In snuba, `sample_weight` on the errors/discover storage is Nullable and is only populated for error events that carry a client sample rate; error events ingested before a project was allowlisted, from SDKs that don't sample, or server-side have NULL `sample_weight`. ClickHouse `sum()` ignores NULL rows and returns NULL if every row is NULL, so (a) any unsampled error events are silently excluded from the returned count (e.g. 10 unsampled errors + 1 error sampled at 0.1 returns 10 instead of the correct 20), and (b) a time bucket containing only unsampled events returns NULL/0 instead of the true count. The added tests never exercise events without a client_sample_rate, so this is not caught. The aggregate should treat missing weights as 1, e.g. `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`; the code comment's assumption that sample_weight always exists for allowlisted projects is not guaranteed by the schema.

findings.title: _is_error_focused_query substring-matches event.type:error, misfiring on negations and quoted text
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` decides whether to rewrite `count()` into `sum(sample_weight)` by checking `if "event.type:error" in query.lower()`. This substring test ignores search semantics: a discover query like `!event.type:error` (the standard way to select transaction-like events) contains the substring and will be treated as error-focused, so its `count()` is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over non-error rows that have no sample_weight — returning NULL/incorrect counts. A free-text search such as `message:"event.type:error"` also false-positives. For allowlisted projects this silently returns wrong data on common discover queries; the check should parse the query and inspect the actual event.type filter (including its negation) rather than doing a substring match.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is computed from the outer `dataset` and raw request query instead of the scoped dataset and query actually executed
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, ...)`, the eligibility check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` using the closure variable `dataset` from `get()`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument, and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`/`_is_error_focused_query` re-read `request.GET["query"]` instead of the `query` argument. The dashboard-widget split path calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., split_query, ...)` where `split_query` is rewritten to `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction`; that error-only query is never upsampled because the decision was made against the original (metrics) dataset and the unmodified request query. The transform decision should be based on the dataset and query string actually being executed, otherwise upsampling is silently skipped (or could be misapplied) for exactly the requests the function arguments describe.

findings.title: Cache key built with Python hash() of project ids is collision-prone
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Python's `hash()` is not collision-free: two different project-id sets within the same organization can produce the same hash and therefore share a cache entry, causing the wrong allowlist eligibility (and thus wrong counts) to be served for up to 60 seconds. The key should encode the ids directly (e.g. comma-joined sorted ids) rather than a hash digest of them.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code; allowlist changes have no invalidation path
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache(organization_id, project_ids)` is introduced with a docstring saying it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing in this PR (or elsewhere) calls it, and there is no signal/hook wired to the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. As shipped, every allowlist change takes up to the full 60-second TTL to take effect with no supported way to invalidate. Either wire the invalidation to the option update path or remove the unused helper and rely on the documented TTL.

findings.title: No tests for the caching behavior that is the PR's stated performance optimization
findings.body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`); the main entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — which contains the new 60-second cache, the cache key construction, and the interaction between cached eligibility and the per-request dataset/query check — is never called. Cache hit/miss behavior, the TTL, and stale-cache regressions (the headline "performance optimization" of this PR) are therefore completely unverified.
